notes: CIRCUIT: single series loop (1.25H inductor - parallel block - 0.75F cap - 15V source - 150ohm resistor) with a three-branch parallel block in the middle: 3A I-DC on top (y~369), 100ohm resistor in the middle (y~447), 1A I-DC on the bottom (y~540), all strung between a left vertical rail at x~334 and a right vertical rail at x~660. NET MAP: n1 = left rail of the parallel block (x~334, y 357..537) = inductor right lead (2.1), left lead of the 3A source (0.0), left lead of the 100ohm resistor (3.0), left lead of the 1A source (4.0). n2 = right rail of the parallel block (x~660, y 357..537) = right leads of 3A (0.1), 100ohm (3.1), 1A (4.1) plus the left plate of the 0.75F capacitor (1.0) via the y~443 horizontal. n3 = right plate of the capacitor (1.1) -> right vertical at x~823 -> bottom rail at y~632 -> '+' (right) terminal of the 15V source (5.1). n4 = left lead of the inductor (2.0) -> left vertical at x~128 -> left lead of the 150ohm resistor (6.0). n5 = right lead of the 150ohm resistor (6.1) -> '-' (left) terminal of the 15V source (5.0). JUDGEMENT CALLS: S14 at (334,450) and S12 at (660,443) are both plain 4-way crossings of the main y~447 horizontal with the vertical rails of the parallel block; S12 shows a distinct thickened blob at the crossing (dot=2.1) and S14 is a clean cross with mild thickening. Both are read as JUNCTIONS. Electrical-impossibility argument, independent of the ink: if either were a crossing, the 3A and the 1A current sources would end up in series in a loop of their own (their two rails joined only at the other end), which is an impossible constraint (3A != 1A), and the parallel block would also be stranded from the rest of the loop. Junction at both is the only sane reading, and it also matches the drafter's habit on this sheet - nowhere on this drawing is a hop or a jog drawn, so a bare crossing means connected. Remaining sites S1, S2, S8, S9, S11, S17, S18 are all handwriting ink ('3A', '1.25H', '1A' labels) brushing a wire and change nothing; left at their defaults. COMPONENTS: all 7 are 2-terminal, all classes agree with the drawing (two I-DC circles with arrows, one V-DC circle with -/+ marks, capacitor, inductor, two resistors); every terminal sits on a real lead in the _comps montage - the extra unused port candidates flagged by the warnings are all strokes of the handwritten value labels ('3A' over the 3A source, '1.25H' over the inductor, '100' under the 100ohm resistor, '1A' under the 1A source, '15V' under the source, '150' over the 150ohm resistor) and none of them are needed. No pin-order questions (no 3-terminal parts). No GND symbol in this drawing, so there is no net '0'. Nothing left unresolved.
